newsitem.title: USA: LDC debts mixed despite U.S. Treasury gains.
newsitem.headline: LDC debts mixed despite U.S. Treasury gains.

text.p: Emerging market debts failed to get much boost from rallying Treasuries as the long-baond yield fell to 6.45 percent, lowest in eight months.
The reluctance to follow the Treasuries mirrored a similar trend in other high yield assets, where spreads have also been widening, said Tulio Vera, Brady bond strategist at Bear Stearns.
"Emerging market debts are in a holding pattern," he said, noting that there was little new momentum to break to new highs after the October correction.
Many cross-over buyers seeking high yields were content sitting on the gains made so far this year and did not want to risk new positions, he said.
Ecuador benefited from continued speculation on launching a currency convertibility plan inspired by Argentina's example.
At 1615 EST/2115 GMT, Ecuador Discounts rose 7/8 to 67-1/8 bid. Ecuador PDI added 1/8 to 58.00.
Vera of Bear Stearns said a full-fledged currency board is premature. Clarification is expected when the government presents Congress with its economic plan November 21, he said.
A more plausible explanation for investors' recent swooning is that as a laggard in the previous rally Ecuador still has some catch-up to do, Vera said.
Brazil underperformed the market amid worries about trade deficits despite attempts by the government to calm the nerves, traders said.
After reporting a trade deficit of $655 million in September, Brazil is expected to chalk up another large monthly shortfall in October.

Finance Minister Pedro Malan in a Reuters interview on Monday said the trade gap in a single month should not be projected over the long term. He estimated that the fiscal deficit would be between 3.7 to four percent of gross domestic product, down from 5.0 percent in 1995.
Argentina appeared to benefit from Brazil's woes as investors switched between assets of the two countries.
While Argentina FRBs slipped 1/8 to 83-5/8 bid, Argentina Pars gained 61-3/8 bid.
Russia enjoyed solid support, although the delay in the deal with London Club of bank creditors and uncertainty over its 1997 budget dampened some enthusiasm, traders said.

"But there were no sellers," said a European bank trader. The Eurobond bond launch, expected between November 22 and 24, and President Boris Yeltsin's recovery from heart surgery provide the underpinnings, he noted.
Russia dollar-denominated Vnesh loan edged 1/8 to 79-3/8 bid.
